chunks: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Muktattib narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated to me from his father, Abi Abdillah Ja'far al-Himyari, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said: I heard Aba Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
Indeed, one who strives with the Quran to memorize it, due to difficulty with it and weakness of his memory, will have two rewards.
And he said: What prevents a merchant among you who is occupied in his market, when he returns to his home, from not sleeping until he recites a Surah from the Quran?
So it is recorded for him, in place of every verse he recites, ten good deeds, and ten bad deeds are erased from him.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for struggling to memorize the Quran and reciting before sleep?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the virtue of *mushqah* (struggle) in memorization, granting double reward to those who exert effort despite weak retention, thereby validating the spiritual worth of diligence over innate ease. He further extends this encouragement to busy merchants, promising ten good deeds and the erasure of ten sins for each verse recited before sleep, linking daily commercial life with consistent spiritual maintenance.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.) said, “One who tries to memorize the  Holy  Quran  with  extreme  difficulty  due  to  a  weak memory will get two rewards.” He further said,
“Why don’t the  people  who  trade  in  markets  whole  day  not  recite  a Surah when they return to their homes at night before going to bed?
If they do so they would get ten rewards for each verse and ten sins will be wiped off.”
